label: Operation Serval — Barkhane Axis (Bamako → Gao)
notes: French Serval advance northward from Bamako through Sévaré and Gao; main French counter-offensive axis Jan–Feb 2013.

label: Operation Serval — Western Axis (Bamako → Timbuktu)
notes: French Serval advance along the western axis through Niono and Léré toward Timbuktu; city liberated January 27, 2013.

label: Operation Serval — Gao to Kidal Advance
notes: French special forces advance from Gao to secure Kidal on January 30, 2013. Chadian forces reinforced the position.

label: Jihadist Advance — Gao to Konna (Jan 2013)
notes: AQIM/Ansar Dine/MUJAO advance from Gao southward to Konna on January 10, 2013 — the move that triggered French intervention.

label: Jihadist Second Axis — Gao to Diabaly (Jan 2013)
notes: MUJAO second axis of advance capturing Diabaly on January 14, 2013, threatening the Ségou-Bamako corridor before French airstrikes halted the advance.

label: JNIM Timbuktu Blockade Corridor
notes: JNIM supply-interdiction corridor from Mopti Region northward along the Niger River, cutting road access to Timbuktu since 2023.

label: Katiba Macina Expansion — Mopti to Ségou
notes: Katiba Macina expansion corridor from its Mopti heartland westward into Ségou Region 2015–2019, exploiting Fulani communal grievances.

label: JNIM Western Expansion — Ségou to Kayes (→ Senegal)
notes: JNIM westward expansion from Ségou through Kayes Region toward Mauritania and Senegal borders 2023–2025; multiple attacks on gendarmerie posts.

label: ISGS Expansion into Liptako-Gourma Tri-Border Zone
notes: ISGS expansion from Ménaka base southward into the Liptako-Gourma tri-border zone 2017–2020, establishing the 'triangle of death'.

label: IS-Sahel Expansion into Northern Burkina Faso
notes: IS-Sahel Province expansion southward from the tri-border zone into Burkina Faso's Sahel Region (Dori, Djibo corridor) from 2019.

label: IS-Sahel Attacks in Tillabéri (Niger)
notes: ISGS/IS-Sahel attack corridor from Ménaka eastward into Niger's Tillabéri Region; multiple major base attacks including Tongo Tongo (2017) and Inates (2019).

label: Wagner/Africa Corps Deployment — Bamako to Mopti
notes: Initial Wagner Group deployment from Bamako to Mopti Region in December 2021, the first operational zone after arrival.

label: Wagner/Africa Corps Northward — Mopti to Gao
notes: Wagner Group extending operations northward from Mopti to Gao from early 2022, taking over former French Barkhane operational zones.

label: FAMa/Africa Corps Kidal Offensive Column (Oct–Nov 2023)
notes: FAMa-Wagner column of ~115 vehicles departing Gao October 2, 2023 and advancing to Kidal, capturing the city November 14, 2023.

label: Africa Corps Deployment — Gao to Timbuktu
notes: Africa Corps deployment to Timbuktu airbase after Barkhane withdrawal from Mali. Russian personnel base struck by JNIM June 2, 2025.

label: JNIM Attack Axis — Mopti to Kati (Sept 2024)
notes: JNIM attack column approach route toward Kati garrison near Bamako, September 17, 2024 — first direct attack on the capital area in the conflict.

label: Operation Barkhane Withdrawal — Gao to Niamey (Aug 2022)
notes: Last French Barkhane soldiers cross from Mali into Niger on August 15, 2022, following expulsion by the Malian junta.

label: JNIM Attack — Boulkessi Base (Jun 2025)
notes: JNIM assault route toward Boulkessi military base near the Mali-Burkina Faso border, June 1, 2025; 60+ killed, 220 taken hostage.

label: JNIM Coordinated Assault — Timbuktu (Jun 2025)
notes: JNIM multi-point coordinated assault on Timbuktu including the Russian Africa Corps airbase, June 2, 2025; 60+ FAMa killed.

label: MNLA Advance — Kidal to Aguelhok (Jan 2012)
notes: MNLA initial offensive axis capturing Aguelhok January 17–24, 2012; site of massacre of ~82 Malian soldiers.

label: Rebel Sweep — Kidal to Gao (Mar 2012)
notes: MNLA and MUJAO sweep from the Kidal-Tessalit axis southward to capture Gao on March 31, 2012, exploiting the political vacuum after the coup.

label: JNIM Cross-Border Expansion — Mali to Burkina Faso
notes: JNIM/Katiba Macina expansion from Mopti Region southward across the Mali-Burkina Faso border 2016–2020, establishing logistics and recruitment networks in northern Burkina Faso.

label: JNIM Expansion — Burkina Faso East toward Niger
notes: JNIM/IS-Sahel eastward expansion from Burkina Faso's Est Region toward Niger's Dosso and Tillabéri border areas from 2019.

label: JNIM Southward Expansion — Burkina to Benin/W Park
notes: JNIM/IS-Sahel southward expansion from Fada N'Gourma toward the W National Park zone and Benin/Togo border areas 2021–2025.

label: ISGS Ambush — Ménaka to Tongo Tongo (Oct 2017)
notes: ISGS attack trajectory for the October 4, 2017 ambush near Tongo Tongo, Niger that killed 4 US Special Forces.

label: France Withdrawal — Niamey to N'Djamena (2023)
notes: France's phased withdrawal of 1,500 troops from Niger to N'Djamena, Chad following the Niger junta's expulsion demand in 2023.

label: FAMa/Africa Corps Supply Axis — Gao to Tessalit
notes: FAMa and Africa Corps logistical supply line from Gao northward to Tessalit following MINUSMA withdrawal and Kidal capture.

label: JNIM Convoy Ambush Corridor — Gao-Bourem Road
notes: JNIM repeated ambush corridor on the Gao-Bourem road and surrounding areas 2022–2024; FAMa convoys regularly targeted.

label: JNIM Siege Corridor — Ouagadougou to Djibo
notes: JNIM blockade of road access from Ouagadougou northward toward Djibo, forcing the Sahel Region provincial capital to rely entirely on costly airlifts for resupply.

label: JNIM Blockade — Kaya to Dori Road
notes: JNIM interdiction of the Kaya-Dori road — the main supply artery to Burkina Faso's Sahel Region — repeatedly ambushed from 2022, accelerating humanitarian collapse.

label: FAMa/Africa Corps Airstrike — Ménaka Region (Mar 26, 2026)
notes: FAMa airstrike on IS-Sahel encampment ~38 km northwest of Ménaka. FAMa claimed 50+ IS-Sahel militants neutralized, entire base destroyed. Third FAMa engagement in the Ménaka theater in one week. High-value ISGS target Abou Alghabhas Ichmali reportedly eliminated in concurrent raid.

label: IS-Sahel Motorcycle Attack — Inkadevan, North Ménaka (Mar 27, 2026)
notes: IS-Sahel motorcycle-mounted fighters attacked a FAMa patrol in the Inkadevan area north of Ménaka before withdrawing. FAMa helicopter gunships struck retreating attackers in the Tinfadimat area. Part of ongoing IS-Sahel counter-pressure against FAMa in the Ménaka theater.

label: IS-Sahel Attack — Sanama, Tillabéri Niger (Mar 25, 2026)
notes: IS-Sahel attack on Niger Army positions at Sanama, Tillabéri Region, killing 6 soldiers. Part of sustained IS-Sahel pressure in western Niger's Liptako-Gourma zone following US military withdrawal from Nigerien bases in 2024.

label: JNIM Attack — Bagade Military Post, Northern Burkina (Mar 22, 2026)
notes: JNIM assault on Bagade military post in northern Burkina Faso killed at least 14 soldiers (possibly up to 20 including VDP). JNIM released video of dead soldiers. Part of a campaign of 30+ attacks in Burkina Faso since February 2026, killing 120+ security forces.

label: FLA FPV Drone Strike — Africa Corps Camp, Tessalit (Apr 1, 2026)
notes: Front de Libération de l'Azawad (FLA/Tuareg separatists) destroyed a Russian Africa Corps camp near Tessalit/Amachach using FPV kamikaze drones. The FLA also struck a TB2 drone control center in the Tessalit area. Continuation of the FLA's sustained asymmetric drone campaign against FAMa/Africa Corps positions following the fall of Kidal in November 2023.

label: FAMa/Africa Corps Airstrike — SE Kidal, Operation Dugukoloko (Apr 2, 2026)
notes: FAMa airstrike on militant positions southeast of Kidal as part of Operation Dugukoloko (March 21–April 3, 2026). FAMa claimed several dozen militants killed, ~10 motorcycles and drone assets destroyed. Africa Corps air assets supported the 13-day ground-air operation.

label: JNIM IED Attack — Kugo to Tonka Patrol Route (Apr 6, 2026)
notes: JNIM detonated 2 IEDs on a joint FAMa/Africa Corps patrol between Kugo and Tonka, Timbuktu Region, killing at least 1 FAMa soldier. JNIM maintains active IED interdiction capabilities along Niger River patrol routes in this region.

label: FLA FPV Drone Strikes — Agelhok FAMa Base (Apr 8, 2026)
notes: FLA (Azawad Liberation Front) launched two FPV kamikaze drone strikes on a FAMa base at Agelhok, Kidal Region. First drone failed to detonate; second narrowly missed a soldier. Part of the FLA's sustained asymmetric drone campaign against FAMa/Africa Corps positions across northern Mali in 2026.

label: ISGS vs. JNIM Clashes — Tillabéri Niger (Apr 2026)
notes: First documented direct armed confrontation between IS-Sahel Province (ISGS) and JNIM inside Niger territory. ISGS claimed killing 35 JNIM operatives on April 2, 2026; JNIM retaliated April 5; clashes continued through mid-April with 50+ fighters killed on both sides per Pravda Mali Apr 4–17 summary. Represents geographic spread of the JNIM-ISGS rivalry from Mali and Burkina Faso into Niger's Tillabéri Region — a historically contested corridor along the tri-border zone where ISGS operated from Ménaka.

label: FAB Strike — Nakamba Sector, Centre-Est (Apr 2026)
damage: JNIM emir Karim Torodo (Abdul Bashir) eliminated; additional fighters neutralized
notes: FAB operation in Nakamba sector, east-central Burkina Faso. Eliminated JNIM field commander Karim Torodo (alias Abdul Bashir, age 35), who had been wanted since June 2023 with a 175M CFA franc reward. Part of FAB's April 2026 counterinsurgency campaign across multiple theaters including the April 13–14 Soum Province operation.

label: FAB Air-Ground Strike — NE Arbinda, Soum Province (Apr 13–14, 2026)
damage: ~100 militants killed, fuel depot and vehicle convoy destroyed; ~50 motorcycles seized
notes: Combined FAB air and ground operation beginning night of April 13. 28th Rapid Intervention Battalion deployed at dawn for sweep. FAB claims ~100 militants neutralized northeast of Arbinda — among the largest single-operation FAB success in 2026. Launched from Ouagadougou-area airbase toward Soum Province target area. Casualty figures are government-claimed; independent verification not possible due to media access restrictions.
platform: FAB combat aircraft + BIR-28 ground units

label: FAMa Airstrike — NW of Dioura, Mopti Region (Apr 23, 2026)
casualties: 60+ JNIM/Katiba Macina fighters KIA (FAMa DIRPA claim)
notes: FAMa precision airstrikes on a major Katiba Macina stronghold northwest of Dioura, Mopti Region. General Staff statement cited 'air vectors mobilized to conduct targeted strikes' against 'a strategic refuge of terrorist groups.' One of the largest single-operation neutralization claims by FAMa in 2026. FAMa DIRPA announced operation April 23; combat aircraft sorties launched from Bamako area. Independent verification not possible.

label: IS-Sahel Attack on Tessit — FAMa Repels (Apr 23, 2026)
notes: IS-Sahel (ISGS/Wilayat Sahel) attack on the town of Tessit, Ansongo Department, Gao Region. FAMa successfully repelled the assault. Approximately 10 motorcycles and weapons seized; IS-Sahel fighters killed and captured. FAMa continued operations in the area. Tessit is a historically significant IS-Sahel attack site (August 2022 attack killed 42). Operation came amid the broader ISGS-JNIM inter-jihadist clashes in Tillabéri in April 2026.

label: JNIM Offensive Column — Mopti to Kati/Bamako (Apr 25, 2026)
notes: JNIM attack axis toward Kati military base and Bamako airport area, April 25, 2026. Two loud explosions and sustained gunfire erupted before 6:00 AM GMT near Kati base, home of junta leader Gen. Assimi Goïta. Defense Minister Sadio Camara's residence in Kati was attacked and severely damaged; his fate was unknown at time of reporting. An AP journalist heard sustained heavy weapons fire near Modibo Keïta International Airport (~15 km from city center), where an Africa Corps camp is located. Four Reuters security sources confirmed JNIM involvement. FAMa deployed soldiers to block roads, helicopters patrolled the airport area. Part of the largest coordinated offensive in Mali since 2012-2013.

label: FLA Offensive — Tessalit Area to Kidal (Apr 25, 2026)
notes: Front de Libération de l'Azawad (FLA/Azawad Liberation Front) Tuareg rebels advanced on Kidal on April 25, 2026, claiming control of 'most of Kidal' including one of two military camps in the city. FLA spokesperson Mohamed Elmaouloud Ramadane announced on social media that the town of Kidal had 'come under the control of our armed forces.' Kidal had been captured by FAMa/Wagner in November 2023 after 11 years of Tuareg control. The April 25 FLA offensive coordinated with simultaneous JNIM attacks on Bamako/Kati and Gao, representing the broadest coordinated militant-separatist operation since 2012. JNIM and FLA are not formally allied but operated in parallel. The situation was described by analysts as 'unprecedented in scale and coordination.'

label: FLA Advance — Anéfis to Gao (Apr 25, 2026)
notes: FLA (Azawad Liberation Front) forces claimed control of positions in Gao on April 25, 2026, simultaneous with their Kidal offensive and coordinated with JNIM attacks on Bamako/Kati. The FLA advance toward Gao represents a strike at the FAMa/Africa Corps operational hub for northern Mali. UN security note confirmed 'simultaneous complex attacks' in Gao as part of the nationwide coordinated offensive. Reuters could not independently verify FLA's territorial claims in Gao at time of reporting.

label: Africa Corps Withdrawal — Kidal to Gao Under FLA Escort (Apr 26, 2026)
notes: Russia's Africa Corps and FAMa soldiers besieged at Camp 2 (former MINUSMA camp) in Kidal since April 25 agreed to withdraw under armed FLA escort on April 26, 2026. A convoy assembled at the camp entrance and departed southward under rebel supervision. FLA declared Kidal 'totally' under its control, with fighters seen at the National Youth Camp and governor's residence. This represents the largest single territorial loss for the Mali junta and Russia's Africa Corps since their joint deployment began in December 2021 — reversing the November 2023 Kidal capture in under 24 hours.

label: Africa Corps Full Withdrawal — Aguelhok/Tessalit to Anéfis (Apr 27, 2026)
notes: April 27, 2026: Russia's Africa Corps officially confirmed via Telegram its withdrawal from Aguelhok and Tessalit — the two remaining major positions in the Kidal Region after Kidal itself fell April 26. Mali's Army Chief of Staff confirmed forces had repositioned to Anéfis. The withdrawal from Aguelhok (approx. 0.97°E, 19.47°N) to Anéfis (1.72°E, 17.65°N) removes all Africa Corps presence from the Kidal Region, reversing the entire November 2023 northern Mali advance.

label: JNIM Captures Tessit — FAMa Negotiated Surrender (Apr 27, 2026)
notes: JNIM seized Tessit (Ansongo Department, Gao Region) on April 27, 2026 after the Malian army agreed to surrender their weapons in exchange for safe passage. This was the second negotiated capitulation in 48 hours, following Kidal (April 26), showing a pattern of FAMa positions collapsing without sustained resistance.

label: ISGS Seizes Labbezanga Border Fort — Niger Closes Crossing (Apr 27, 2026)
notes: Islamic State – Sahel Province (ISSP) seized the Labbezanga border fort after Malian troops abandoned the post and fled toward Ansongo. Labbezanga sits at the Mali-Niger border crossing on the Niger River. ISSP's advance from the Ménaka area (2.40°E, 15.92°N) westward toward Labbezanga (0.31°E, 15.04°N) cuts a key transit route between northeastern Mali and western Niger. Niger closed its Mali border in response.

label: JNIM Bamako Siege Blockade — Supply Route Interdiction (Apr 28–, 2026)
notes: JNIM 'total siege' of Bamako announced April 28, 2026 by spokesman Abu Hudheifah al-Bambari. US Embassy confirmed April 30 that hundreds of vehicles are stranded at multiple city entry points. JNIM controls supply routes from the Mopti corridor (primary axis shown) plus Gao-Bamako route and southern roads. JNIM coalition manifesto May 1 calls for FAMa defections to accelerate the siege. Builds on March 2026 fuel blockade that ended with prisoner release deal; new siege declared following April 25–30 offensive.

label: JNIM Motorcycle Attack — Bagare VDP Post, Passor Province (May 2, 2026)
notes: JNIM motorcycle-mounted assault on VDP (Volunteers for the Defense of the Motherland) post at Bagare in northern Burkina Faso's Passor province. Attack lasted over one hour. At least 11 VDP volunteers killed; shops, vehicles, and motorcycles set ablaze. JNIM claimed 'taking control of a military post belonging to the Burkinabe militias.' Part of sustained JNIM pressure across the Sahel simultaneously with the Mali siege.

label: ISGS Seizes Urban Ménaka — FAMa Retreats to Former UN Base (Apr 28, 2026)
notes: ISSP (Islamic State – Sahel Province) seized the urban area of Ménaka on April 28, 2026. Malian Army and Africa Corps units retreated to the fortified former UN peacekeeping camp on the western outskirts. IS fighters occupied the local administration building, set up checkpoints, and spent the night in government facilities. FAMa and Africa Corps remain besieged in the base. The seizure of Ménaka's urban core — combined with JNIM's Bamako siege and FLA's Kidal consolidation — means the Mali state has effectively lost control of all major cities north of the Niger River within 72 hours.

label: JNIM Assault — Kenieroba Central Prison, 60km SW of Bamako (May 6–7, 2026)
damage: Prison perimeter breached; supply convoys to Bamako set ablaze; FAMa repelling assault as of latest reports
notes: JNIM fighters launched a ground assault on Kenieroba Central Prison ('Africa's Alcatraz') on May 6–7, 2026. The prison holds 2,500 inmates including 72+ high-value JNIM detainees arrested following the April 25 offensive. Simultaneously, JNIM burned food supply convoys heading to Bamako and established checkpoints around the capital — reinstating supply siege tactics that the May 2 convoy breakthrough had broken. FAMa actively repelling the assault. Line represents JNIM attack vector from blockade positions north of Bamako toward the prison SW of the capital.

label: JNIM Assault — Djibo Provincial Capital (May 11, 2026)
notes: JNIM hundreds of fighters assault Djibo, Burkina Faso's Sahel Region capital, beginning 5:00 AM May 11, 2026. 9-hour occupation (5AM–2PM). Army camp seized and looted; gendarmerie HQ, police HQ, hospital, market burned. At least 26 civilians summarily executed; women abducted. Fighter jet turned back by JNIM fire; drones not deployed. Helicopter-borne reinforcements arrived after JNIM withdrawal. ICG: 'Major jihadist attack exposes military failings in Burkina Faso.' Line represents JNIM attack approach from northern corridor toward Djibo center.

label: FAMa Airstrike — ISSP Motorcycle Column, Ménaka Region (May 12, 2026)
damage: ISSP motorcycle column targeted; Ménaka urban standoff ongoing
notes: FAMa airstrike on ISSP motorcycle fighters in Ménaka Region, May 12, 2026. Part of ongoing effort to degrade ISSP mobility around Ménaka city, where ISSP seized the urban core April 28 and forced FAMa/Africa Corps to retreat to the fortified former UN camp. ISSP withdrew from city center but continues mortar fire on the besieged base. Aircraft depart from Gao (shown) — main FAMa/Africa Corps air hub for northern Mali. Casualty figures not confirmed.

label: JNIM Attack — Porga Military Post, Northern Benin (May 7, 2026)
casualties: 7 Beninese soldiers killed; weapons and motorcycles seized
notes: JNIM motorcycle-mounted fighters attacked a military post in Porga district, Atacora Department, northern Benin (~30 km from Burkina Faso border) on approximately May 7, 2026. 7 soldiers killed, weapons and motorcycles seized. Represents continued JNIM southward expansion toward Gulf of Guinea states from Burkina Faso's Est Region. Attack approach corridor shown from Ouagadougou area (JNIM staging zone) to Porga. Benin has faced escalating jihadist infiltration in the W-Arly-Pendjari (WAP) complex zone since 2021. Confirmed by Pravda Burkina Faso (May 11, 2026).

label: JNIM Twin Village Massacres — Mopti Region (May 8, 2026)
notes: JNIM simultaneous night raids on Korikori and Gomossogou villages, Mopti Region, central Mali, night of May 6–7 (reported May 8, 2026). Fighters opened fire, ransacked homes, and torched properties. Toll: at least 30 (AFP) to 50+ (WAMAPS/diplomatic sources). JNIM cited Dan Na Ambassagou (DNA) self-defense militia cooperation with FAMa as justification. FAMa subsequently launched a counter-operation killing approximately 12 JNIM fighters. Line shows JNIM attack approach from Katiba Macina core zone (Djenné area) toward the massacre villages NE of Mopti's central district.

label: AES Joint Air Operations — Central Mali (May 2026)
damage: JNIM Katiba Macina logistics and command posts targeted in central Mali
casualties: Unknown; AES has not released confirmed figures
notes: Alliance of Sahel States joint air campaign in Malian territory confirmed from May 1, 2026 (Africanews), with operations continuing as of May 18. Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger air assets coordinate via the AES Unified Force Command (CCEMC). Operations target JNIM logistics corridors and command posts primarily across the Mopti-Ségou operational belt — JNIM's Katiba Macina heartland. The AES joint operations represent the first meaningful deployment of the joint force inaugurated December 2025 and expanded to 15,000 authorized troops in April 2026. Origin shown from Ouagadougou (FAB operations coordination hub); target area is central Mali Mopti corridor.
platform: FAMa/FAB/FAN combat aircraft (coordinated AES joint command)

label: JNIM Assault — Diapaga, Est Region, Burkina Faso (May 12–13, 2026)
notes: JNIM overran the army outpost at Diapaga, capital of Tapoa Province in Burkina Faso's Est Region, on May 12–13, 2026. 50+ soldiers and VDP volunteers killed; buildings and monuments destroyed; prison inmates released (including suspected jihadists); weapons and equipment seized before JNIM withdrawal. Diapaga was the last major FAB buffer before the Togolese border (~25 km away), threatening the Lomé–Fada N'Gourma–Ouagadougou commercial corridor. Part of JNIM's coordinated southeastern Burkina Faso offensive arc: Djibo (May 11, Sahel Region) → Diapaga (May 13, Est Region) → Diabou (May 14, Gourma). Source: Zagazola Makama (May 13, 2026). Line shows JNIM approach from Est Region JNIM network staging area toward Diapaga.

label: FAMa Drone Strike — Tene, San Region (May 18, 2026)
damage: Civilian motorbike procession struck; wedding gathering targeted
notes: FAMa drones struck a motorbike procession of villagers gathering for a traditional collective wedding ceremony in Tene locality, San District, Ségou Region, central Mali. AFP wire confirmed 10+ civilian deaths. A security source told AFP the drones targeted 'a procession of motorbikes following one another' — the same movement pattern as JNIM logistics convoys in the Mopti-Ségou belt. Malian junta issued no statement. Strike origin shown from Sévaré airfield (closest FAMa drone-capable airbase to the strike area). Source: Al Jazeera / AFP, May 18, 2026.

label: FAMa/AES Airstrikes — FLA/JNIM-Held Kidal (May 20, 2026)
damage: FLA/JNIM logistics and command nodes in Kidal targeted; civilian infrastructure at risk
casualties: Unknown; FLA has not released figures
notes: Mali's Armed Forces (FAMa) and Africa Corps launched repeated drone and air strikes on JNIM/FLA-held Kidal over several days preceding May 20, 2026, per Foreign Policy analysis. Kidal was seized by FLA/JNIM on April 26 during the nationwide offensive that also killed Defence Minister Camara. The aerial campaign represents a shift from failed ground operations to air interdiction following Africa Corps' retreat from all Kidal Region bases to Anéfis. FAMa's DIRPA released military videos of the strikes. City remains under FLA control as of May 21. Strike origin from Gao (main FAMa/Africa Corps operational hub for northern Mali). Source: Foreign Policy, May 20, 2026.
platform: FAMa/Africa Corps armed UAV and combat aircraft

label: JNIM Incursion — Tillabéri, Niger (May 22, 2026)
notes: JNIM claimed an attack in Niger's Tillabéri Region on approximately May 22, 2026 — historically ISGS/IS-Sahel Province territory. The incursion signals JNIM expanding from Burkina Faso staging areas into western Niger to contest ISGS territorial dominance in the Tillabéri corridor. Combined with the April 2026 ISGS-JNIM armed clashes (50+ killed), this marks a new phase of inter-jihadist competition for the tri-border zone. Line shows approximate JNIM axis from Burkina Faso staging zone toward Tillabéri. Single Tier-3 source; confidence low. Source: The Authority News, May 22, 2026.

label: Africa Corps Alleged Cluster Bomb — Tadjmart/Aguelhoc Area, Kidal Region (May 16–17, 2026)
damage: ShOAB-0.5 submunitions scattered across cultivated land and nomadic routes; cluster munitions confirmed by RFI weapons specialist
notes: RFI weapons specialist identified Russian-made RBK-500 cluster bomb delivery system and ShOAB-0.5 submunitions in Tadjmart hamlet near Aguelhoc. Story broke May 23, 2026 based on May 16-17 incident. Second strike reported near Oubder (In-Gouzma, Timbuktu Region). Africa Corps and Mali are non-signatories to the Convention on Cluster Munitions. FLA collecting unexploded remnants as evidence.

label: JNIM Attack — Titao-Sollé Trading Convoy, Loroum Province (May 29, 2026)
notes: JNIM motorcycle-borne attack on trading convoy along the Titao-Sollé axis in Loroum Province, Nord Region, Burkina Faso; at least 15 civilians killed. Approach from Sahel Region Djibo corridor.

label: JNIM Ambush — ICRC Aid Convoy, Barsalogho (May 29–30, 2026)
notes: JNIM ambush of ICRC aid convoy returning from Foube refugee camp near Barsalogho, Sanmatenga Province. 13 killed (5 gendarmes + 5+ civilians including ICRC ambulance driver and nurse), 40 wounded. IHL violation targeting protected humanitarian personnel.

label: JNIM Market Massacre — Kompienbiga, Est Region (May 31, 2026)
notes: Armed militants on motorcycles attacked Kompienbiga livestock market in Kompienga Province, Est Region, Burkina Faso; ~30 civilians killed. Attack from Diapaga (seized May 13) southward toward Kompienga Province. Eid al-Adha period targeted attack on market gathering.

label: FAMa/Africa Corps Counteroffensive — Claimed Labbezanga Recapture (Jun 1, 2026)
damage: Labbezanga border fort claimed recaptured from ISSP; concurrent airstrike on militant camp claimed
casualties: 60+ militants neutralized (FAMa/Africa Corps claim — single Russian-aligned source, unverified)
notes: FAMa and Africa Corps (Pravda Mali, June 1, 2026) claimed to have 'regained control of several sections of the border' including Labbezanga — seized by ISSP on April 27, 2026. Africa Corps also claimed an airstrike on a terrorist camp. All claims originate from Pravda Mali (Russian state-aligned); no Tier 1-2 independent corroboration as of June 2. Confidence: LOW. If confirmed, Labbezanga recapture would be the first reversal of an April 2026 ISSP territorial gain. Line shows FAMa counteroffensive axis from Gao toward Labbezanga border position.
platform: FAMa/Africa Corps ground forces and combat aircraft

label: JNIM IED — Bamako–Kayes Highway Landmine, 8 Killed (Jun 1, 2026)
notes: JNIM-planted landmine struck a passenger bus on the Bamako–Kayes highway near Kita area on June 1, 2026. The western trade corridor connecting Bamako to Senegal and Mauritania. Line represents JNIM siege interdiction axis westward from Bamako. ISS Africa (June 4) identified this corridor as part of JNIM's systematic $26.5M/month economic strangulation campaign against the Dakar-Bamako trade route. Sources: Legit.ng, Sahara Reporters, June 2, 2026.

label: FAMa/Africa Corps Airstrikes — FLA Logistics Nodes, Northern Mali (Jun 4, 2026)
damage: FLA supply lines and logistics nodes in Kidal Region corridor targeted
notes: FAMa and Africa Corps aviation struck FLA (Front de Libération de l'Azawad / Tuareg Liberation Front) logistics nodes in northern Mali on June 4, 2026 — part of the ongoing aerial interdiction campaign against FLA since May 20. Origin: Gao (FAMa/Africa Corps main air hub). Target: Kidal Region logistics corridors through which FLA has resupplied its forces since seizing Kidal on April 26, 2026. FLA chief stated 'Kidal is only the beginning' per The Africa Report. Africa Defense Forum (June 2026): FLA continues gaining ground despite airstrike pressure. Single Tier-3 source (Pravda Mali); confidence medium. Consistent with documented campaign pattern.

label: Africa Corps First Lancet Loitering Munition Strike — Nazarak, Tombouctou Region (Jun 2, 2026)
damage: Pickup truck carrying militants destroyed; direct hit confirmed in released video
notes: Africa Corps released video June 2, 2026 of the first confirmed Lancet loitering munition strike in Mali — targeting a pickup truck carrying militants in Nazarak, Tombouctou Region. Direct hit confirmed in released footage. The Lancet (Russian-manufactured precision loitering munition) has been extensively used in Ukraine; its deployment to Mali marks the introduction of a significantly more capable precision strike asset into the theater, replacing Mi-35 helicopter-based fire support following the April 28 shoot-down. Origin: Africa Corps Timbuktu airbase. Target: Nazarak area, approximately north of Timbuktu (coordinates approximate — Nazarak is a small locality in the region). Source: The Intel Drop, June 2, 2026.

label: FLA-JNIM Offensive — Gao/Aguelhok/Anéfis (Jul 4, 2026)
casualties: Disputed; FLA claimed 2 helicopters shot down and a reinforcement convoy destroyed
notes: FLA-JNIM coalition launched a coordinated three-front offensive on Gao, Aguelhok, and Anéfis beginning ~5:30am July 4, 2026. FAMa/Africa Corps repelled the Gao and Aguelhok attacks; the most intense fighting concentrated on Anéfis, a key waypoint on the Kidal-Bourem-Gao supply route. FLA claimed full control of the Anéfis base — classified low-confidence pending independent verification. Sustained clashes continued roughly six days. Sources: Critical Threats (Jul 9), France24, Al Jazeera.

label: FAMa/Africa Corps Counteroffensive — Anéfis Recapture Claimed (Jul 8–10, 2026)
damage: Malian authorities claimed 54 airstrikes over Anéfis Jul 6–8; a resupply column of ~67 armored vehicles was IED-ambushed near Tabrichat Jul 7–9
casualties: Government claim: 300+ insurgents killed (unverified). Separately reported: ~30 FAMa dead, 60 wounded, ~100 militants claimed killed, 12 vehicles destroyed in the recapture operation (reported Jul 12).
notes: Sources disagree on the exact recapture date — Critical Threats (tier 3) says government forces retook Anéfis by Jul 8–9; other wire reporting frames it as occurring around Jul 10. Casualty figures are government claims, largely unverified by independent monitors. Two Il-76 transports flew in reinforcements/matériel on Jul 7.
platform: FAMa/Africa Corps combat aircraft and armored column

label: FLA-JNIM Ambush — Africa Corps Relief Convoy Near Tabrichat (Jul 5–9, 2026)
casualties: 1 Mi-24 helicopter shot down (Jul 5); resupply column IED-ambushed Jul 7–9
notes: An Africa Corps relief convoy from Gao toward the besieged Anéfis garrison was ambushed near Tabrichat on July 5, 2026, with a Mi-24 helicopter shot down. A larger resupply column (~67 armored vehicles plus fuel trucks) was again IED-ambushed near Tabrichat July 7–9. Single tier-3 source (Critical Threats); confidence low pending independent corroboration.

label: First Confirmed Shahed-136-Type Strike — Inafarak, Timbuktu Region (Jul 12, 2026)
notes: Open-source researchers geolocated the first confirmed use of a Shahed-136-type loitering munition (assessed as a likely Russian-manufactured Garpiya-A1 variant) on the Mali battlefield, striking near Inafarak. Exact strike time not specified in sourcing (placeholder). Single-source (Rio Times Online); confidence low pending independent corroboration. Marks direct technology transfer from the Russia-Ukraine battlefield into the Sahel theater.

label: Second Shahed-136-Type Strike — Talahandak, Northern Mali (Jul 17, 2026)
notes: Second confirmed Shahed-136-type/Garpiya-A1 loitering munition strike in Mali, near Talahandak in the far north. Exact strike time not specified in sourcing (placeholder). Single-source (Rio Times Online); confidence low.

label: FLA-JNIM Ambush — FAMa/Africa Corps Convoy Near Tabankort (Jul 17–18, 2026)
casualties: Disputed: ~50 soldiers killed and 20 captured per aggregated reporting; Mali's military did not confirm specific numbers (Al Jazeera)
notes: A joint FLA-JNIM force ambushed a FAMa/Africa Corps convoy traveling from Anéfis to Gao near Tabankort, shortly after government forces claimed to have retaken Anéfis. Both FLA and JNIM separately claimed responsibility and released footage of captured/surrendering soldiers. Mali's army announced a counter-offensive. Sources: Al Jazeera, Washington Times (AP wire).

label: Ambush on Niger Army Detachment — Bankilaré–Téra Axis, Tillabéri (Jul 17, 2026)
casualties: Official (Niger MoD): 16 killed, 23 wounded. Unofficial (RFI, relayed): 47+ killed including unit commander, 50+ wounded — nearly 3x the official figure.
notes: Niger Armed Forces liaison detachment ambushed near Doungouro village on the Bankilaré–Téra road — contested ground between ISSP/ISGS and JNIM; attacker identity not officially confirmed. African Union Commission condemned the attack Jul 18, citing a 'resurgence of terrorist attacks across the Sahel.' Casualty figures heavily disputed between official and unofficial sources.

label: JNIM Assault — FAMa Barracks, San, Ségou Region (Aug 9, 2026)
casualties: At least 10 soldiers killed (AFP); Mali's military claims ~40 militants killed in response (disputed, unverified)
notes: JNIM fighters attacked and temporarily occupied FAMa's main barracks in San, Ségou Region — well south of the historical northern front line, closer to Bamako's approaches. JNIM claimed 'full control' of the barracks; Mali's military said it conducted a 'vigorous riposte' and had the situation 'under control.' Sources: AFP wire via NAMPA and Club of Mozambique.

label: FAMa/Africa Corps 'Operation Dougoukoloko' — Kidal/Abeibara Interdiction (Aug 3–4, 2026)
damage: Aug 3: JNIM weapons/logistics stocks detected near Abeibara. Aug 4: JNIM logistics/basing infrastructure in Kidal city reportedly 'completely destroyed.'
casualties: Unspecified militants reportedly neutralized (single-source government-aligned claim)
notes: Reported solely by a Russian-state-linked outlet (African Initiative); no independent Tier 1-2 corroboration found. Confidence low. Exact strike time not specified in sourcing (placeholder).
platform: FAMa/Africa Corps ground and air forces
